text: {"score":3,"justification":"The summary is mostly accurate and cautious, and its numbers match the card. The inconclusive leaning fits the thin documentation. Several claims are loosely supported, though, and the next steps and cited examples are weaker than the prose suggests. An investigator would have to redo some of the work.","problems":["Headline says 99215 is above expectation \"at every complexity tier\", and the rationale says \"two to four times the all-provider rate in every band\". The card ratios are about 3.6x, 3.0x, 1.9x, 2.0x, 2.5x and 1.8x. Two bands are below 2x, so \"two to four times\" is inaccurate.","\"Sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0185341 (urinary tract infection code only), C0185668 (rash), C0185909 (abdominal pain)\" interprets dx codes (N39.0, R21, R10.9) beyond the card. They are labeled sampled and described as hard to explain, which overreads minimal dx data. The summary never notes that these claims have no documentation.","The next steps are generic and do not match the rationale. The rationale says to first request charts for the listed low-complexity 99215 claims, but next_steps asks for a \"larger sample of 99214 and 99215\" and a re-screen. No specific claim IDs are named in the steps.","The cited examples are poorly chosen. C0185361 is a 99213 below-billed example, which is irrelevant to the 99215 concern. C0185301 is a low-complexity claim with a hypertension dx. The summary's own strongest low-complexity examples (C0185668, C0185909) are not in cited_claim_ids.","\"The heavy concentration in 99214 also merits a look\" is unsupported by any comparison on the card, since there is no peer 99214 rate. Only the 99214 count of 572 of 829 is available.","The 0% below-billed rate on 3 documented 99215 claims against a 9% comparison rate is a very small sample. It is flagged as thin, but the comparison adds little. The 99213 below-billed rate of 25% (1 of 4) is ignored in the rationale except as an example."]}
